subject: FinMark private endpoint TLS: change window, cert sourcing, and rotation plan
messages:
From: security@finmark.io
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: networking@acmepartner.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: TLS setup for finmark-private.redwood.local — requirements and proposed windows

Hi Neha / Monica,

Thanks again for the sync today. As we start preparing for the private deployment handoff we wanted to capture our hard requirements for TLS and a suggested change window so procurement and our security team can align. Attached is a short PDF with our constraints. Key points:

- Certificate sourcing: our security policy prefers organization-validated certs from a public CA (DigiCert) for external endpoints; for purely private FQDNs that resolve only inside our VPC we can accept internal CA certs if they are logged to our PKI and audited.
- mTLS: we require mutual TLS between the customer-facing edge and our runtime for all tenant traffic (mutual auth at TLS layer).
- Rotation: certificates must be rotatable with zero downtime; we need a documented rollback window and a test canary path.
- DNS: split-horizon DNS is expected for the private FQDN (internal zone in FinMark VPC) — please confirm the ownership model and whether Redwood will create SRV records for runtime discovery.

Proposed change window: Friday 2026-06-11 01:00-04:00 UTC (low traffic for FinMark). Please confirm whether Redwood needs any longer maintenance window for cert chain swaps and KV cache warm-up.

Attachments: finmark-tls-requirements.pdf

Regards,
Sam Patel
Security Engineer
FinMark
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: security@finmark.io
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TLS setup for finmark-private.redwood.local — requirements and proposed windows

Thanks Sam — this is clear and helpful. Quick confirmations from our side and proposed implementation notes: 

1) Certificate sourcing: we can support both models. For public-signed certs (DigiCert) we will provision edge certificates on the Redwood-managed sidecar; for internal-only FQDNs we recommend issuing certs from the customer's internal CA and uploading them to our private trust store (we provide a signed CSR flow). We'll document the CSR/PKCS#12 exchange in the onboarding doc.

2) mTLS: Redwood edge proxy will negotiate mTLS to the runtime. Option A (recommended): terminate client-facing TLS at the edge proxy, then re-establish mTLS to the runtime with a short-lived workload cert issued by our internal CA. Option B: terminate TLS at the runtime sidecar directly if FinMark prefers end-to-end. Option A gives better observability.

3) Rotation and rollback: attached is a CSV with a suggested rotation cadence for CA leaf certs and intermediate certs plus automation hooks for Canary rollouts. We'll run the swap in two phases: canary (10% of traffic) then full. If the canary fails we will automatically revert to the previous cert and revert the DNS SRV weights.

4) DNS ownership: we can either (a) manage a split-horizon zone delegated to Redwood nameservers inside FinMark VPC, or (b) FinMark manages the internal zone and creates the SRV/A records we provide. For option (a) we will need a short-lived delegation record and IAM permissions to create the zone.

Please review the attached rotation-table.csv and confirm the change window. If the 11th works we will lock it and raise JIRA INFRA-1876 to track tasks.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, security@finmark.io
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TLS setup for finmark-private.redwood.local — requirements and proposed windows

Neha / Sam — a few technical items to call out that will impact the change sequence and prework: 

- SAN vs wildcard: for internal-only FQDNs we should prefer explicit SAN lists. Wildcards increase blast radius on cert revocation and complicate pinning in bootstrap flows.
- Bootstrap pinning: we should include a short-lived bootstrap cert on the runtime to validate the first connection; after successful mTLS handshake we rotate to the standard workload cert. This avoids circular dependency if DNS or OCSP checks are unreliable in the customer's air-gapped segments.
- OCSP/CRL: FinMark will need to allow OCSP stapling from our edge proxy to their CRL/OCSP endpoints, or we will enable OCSP stapling with our internal stapling cache. If FinMark disallows external OCSP, we will rely on in-band CRL distribution which will increase rotation lead time.
- DNS SRV for runtime discovery: we recommend SRV records with short TTL (30s) during rollout to allow incremental traffic shifting. If FinMark controls the zone, provide a terraform snippet or API token to automate record changes.

Two clarifying questions for Sam: 1) Will FinMark accept an intermediate CA chain issued by DigiCert that chains to a private intermediate (they suggested)? 2) Any constraints on outbound egress from runtime to certificate validation endpoints?

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, security@finmark.io
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TLS setup for finmark-private.redwood.local — requirements and proposed windows

Agree with Karthik. A couple of operational items to include in the runbook: 

- Emergency revocation: document a one-hour emergency revocation playbook that includes (a) immediate DNS rollback to previous record set, (b) update / restart of edge proxies with pinned previous cert, (c) communication template to customer SREs. I attached an outline.
- Key material handling: ensure uploaded PKCS#12 blobs are stored encrypted in our KMS with HSM-wrapped keys; rotation automation must not expose private keys in plaintext in logs.
- Testing: create a short smoke test that validates both TLS handshake (certificate chain and SANs) and mTLS identity on the runtime. The baseline must run before canary cutover.

Attachment: cert-revocation-playbook.md

I recommend we accept DigiCert intermediate + private leaf only if FinMark's security signoff includes an auditable chain and CT logs (where applicable). For purely internal FQDNs we should default to customer-signed leafs or our managed leafs issued from a mutually-agreed internal intermediate.

Marcus Lin
Lead Infrastructure Architect, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: security@finmark.io
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, digicert-sales@digicert.com

Subject: Re: TLS setup for finmark-private.redwood.local — change window confirmation and final decision log

Sam — thanks for the quick reviews and the clarifications everyone provided. Consolidating decisions and next steps so procurement and your platform team can proceed: 

Decisions made
- DNS: FinMark will manage the internal split-horizon zone. Redwood will provide Terraform templates and an API token. We will use SRV records with TTL=30s during rollout.
- Cert sourcing: For finmark-private.redwood.local (internal-only) FinMark will issue leaf certs from their internal CA and upload PKCS#12 bundles to Redwood (encrypted). Redwood will provide the CSR flow if needed.
- mTLS topology: Option A (edge terminates client TLS; mTLS to runtime with short-lived workload cert) is the default. Option B (end-to-end) is available if FinMark requests it explicitly.
- Rotation + rollback: Two-stage rollout (10% canary -> 100%). Automatic revert on canary failure. Emergency revocation playbook agreed.

Action items (owners & timeline)
- FinMark: provide internal CA chain and confirm OCSP/CRL access by 2026-06-09 (Sam)
- Redwood (Karthik): provide terraform snippet and API token instructions by 2026-06-05
- Redwood (Marcus): smoke test and revocation playbook finalization by 2026-06-09
- Redwood (Neha): schedule change window for 2026-06-11 01:00-04:00 UTC and raise JIRA INFRA-1876 (completed)

Change window is now confirmed for 2026-06-11 01:00-04:00 UTC. Please reply if FinMark needs a different window; otherwise we will begin preflight checks the week of June 8th. I've attached the three artifacts referenced in thread.

Thanks all — we will use the linked Google Doc to track runbook edits: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FinMark-TLS-Change-Plan
